sentence: The NHS lists an irregular pulse, palpitations, a fast heartbeat, tiredness and chest tightness among the main signs of atrial fibrillation.
note: NHS page lists irregular pulse, palpitations, fast heartbeat, tiredness, reduced exercise tolerance, chest tightness, breathlessness, dizziness (via blended summary)

sentence: Breathlessness, dizziness and reduced ability to exercise are also listed.
note: same list

sentence: Sometimes there are no symptoms at all.

sentence: In some cases it can be picked up by a pulse check.
note: 'In some cases, atrial fibrillation can be detected by a pulse check' (summary of NHS-family pages)

sentence: NHS inform describes atrial fibrillation as not usually life threatening in itself.
note: 'not usually life threatening in itself'

sentence: It adds that many people live normal healthy lives with the condition.

sentence: The British Heart Foundation (BHF) likewise says there is no cure but people with AF can lead healthy lives.

sentence: NHS inform sorts atrial fibrillation into types by how long the episodes last.
note: classifies AF by episode duration

sentence: Paroxysmal AF comes and goes, with episodes lasting from minutes to hours.
note: paroxysmal: comes and goes, minutes to hours

sentence: Persistent AF is when an episode lasts for more than seven days.
note: persistent: more than 7 days

sentence: Long-standing persistent AF is continuous for over a year.
note: long-standing persistent: over a year

sentence: In permanent AF the heart rhythm does not go back to normal.
note: permanent: rhythm does not revert

sentence: The BHF describes permanent AF as living with the condition long term, even after treatment.

sentence: The NHS says there is currently no cure for atrial fibrillation, but treatment should help manage the symptoms and lower the risk of complications.
